Giotto Suite needs R 4.4.1 or later. Python is optional.

# Install

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("GiottoUtils",
    repos = c("https://giotto-suite.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
GiottoUtils::suite_install(ref = "disk_full", install_arrow = TRUE)
```

This installs Giotto, GiottoData with the tutorial datasets, GiottoDisk for
large datasets, GiottoConnect for other ecosystems and tools, and the optional
speed-ups (GiottoKernels, GiottoIngest, SedonaDB, smotif, edgeicg and others):
everything the tutorials use. The first run builds *arrow* with zstd support
from source, which can take a while.

# More options

<details>
<summary><strong>Lightest install: Giotto and the mini datasets</strong></summary>

Giotto with the example datasets of GiottoData, for data that fits in memory.
Skips GiottoDisk and the *arrow* build, so it installs quickly.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
GiottoUtils::suite_install(c("Giotto", "GiottoData"), ref = "disk")
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Lighter install: Giotto and GiottoDisk only</strong></summary>

Skips the optional speed-ups. They can be added later, one by one.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
GiottoUtils::suite_install("GiottoDisk", install_arrow = TRUE)
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Add a package later</strong></summary>

Any package from the full install can be added on its own, for example
GiottoConnect or smotif and its compiled backend:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
GiottoUtils::suite_install(c("GiottoConnect", "smotif", "smotifrs"),
    suite_deps = FALSE)
```

`suite_deps = FALSE` keeps the Giotto packages you already have.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Release version</strong></summary>

The current release of Giotto. GiottoDisk is not part of a release yet and will
be added in a future one. Some tutorials use functions that are newer than the
release; use the install above to run them.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/Giotto")
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Other branches</strong></summary>

`suite_install()` installs the Giotto Suite modules in the right order from a
chosen set of branches, set with `ref`:

| `ref` | Installs |
|---|---|
| `"main"` (default) | the release branches |
| `"dev"` | the development branches |
| `"disk"` | the branches GiottoDisk builds against |
| `"disk_full"` | `"disk"`, plus GiottoLens and the optional speed-ups |

```{r, eval=FALSE}
GiottoUtils::suite_install(ref = "dev")
```

Add `dry_run = TRUE` to print the install commands without running them. See
the [`suite_install()` reference](https://giotto-suite.github.io/GiottoUtils/reference/suite_install.html)
for all options.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>System requirements</strong></summary>

- **Build tools:** packages installed from GitHub may need the
  [Posit package development prerequisites](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/200486498-Package-Development-Prerequisites)
  for your system.
- **{terra} on Linux:** needs GDAL (>= 2.2.3), GEOS (>= 3.4.0), PROJ (>= 4.9.3)
  and sqlite3. On our AlmaLinux 8 HPC, gdal 3.6.4, geos 3.11.1, proj 9.2.0 and
  sqlite3 3.37.2 work well. See the [{terra} repository](https://github.com/rspatial/terra)
  for details. On Windows and macOS, `install.packages("terra")` is enough.
- **R older than 4.4.1:** the release install (`ref = "main"`) switches to the
  R 4.4.0 branches automatically. On R older than 4.4.0, install {Matrix} 1.6-5 first:
  `remotes::install_version("Matrix", version = "1.6-5")`.

</details>

Python is not needed to install Giotto. A few functions use Python tools,
which install themselves on first use; see
[Python in Giotto Suite](python.html).

# Help

Running into errors? See the [troubleshooting page](troubleshooting.html) or
open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/giotto-suite/Giotto/issues). Please
include your R, Giotto and operating system versions.
